To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sensitivity of real time PCR for the detection and identification of bovine DNA depends on the length of the target sequence and the thermal treatment of the sample material.
real-time PCR is able to detect bovine DNA in MBM, but the sensitivity is dependent on the thermal processing of the MBM.
the detectability in the real-time PCR assay is influenced by the length of the target sequence, by the degree of thermal treatment, and by the quality of the MBM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sensitive and reliable real-time PCR for detecting bovine DNA in mixed feedstuffs.
the question whether the real-time PCR assays are reliable tools for the detection of animal-derived feed ingredients in heat-processed animal feed.
the development of an analytical procedure that can be used for the control of the thermal process of meat and bone meal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sensitivity of the PCR assay for detection of DNA is influenced by the length of the amplified target sequence.
the detection of bovines in heat-sterile feed by real-time PCR is not reliable.
real-time PCR for detection of bovine mt-DNA is not reliable for the detection and quantification of bovine meat in mixed feed, if the meat is processed to a high degree.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PCR assay with the 109 bp target is more suitable for the detection of the correct thermal process of meat and bone meal than the assay amplifying a 271 bp fragment.
the detection of the presence of animal tissues in feedstuffs can be achieved by PCR amplification of mitochondrial DNA segments.
real-time PCR is an excellent method to verify the absence or presence of meat and bone meals in mixed feedstuffs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection of bovin DNA by real-time PCR is influenced by the degree and duration of heat sterilisation of MBM.
the detection of animal-derived materials in mixed feed by real-time PCR depends strongly on the thermal treatment and the length of the target sequence amplified.
the detection of bovines by PCR in feedstuffs is influenced by the degree and duration of the heating process.
